welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the ideologies and wartime conferences that split the world in two.
meta_desc: GCSE History — ideological roots of the Cold War and the Yalta and Potsdam conferences.
final_note: You learned the ideological clash, the wartime conferences, and how mistrust began between the USA and USSR.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The USA was capitalist. The USSR was communist.

They had been allies against Hitler, but their beliefs about politics, the economy and freedom were opposites. After 1945 only these two superpowers remained strong.

Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin met at Yalta in Soviet Crimea.

They agreed Germany would be divided into four zones, the USSR would join the war on Japan, and free elections would happen in liberated Europe — though Stalin meant something different by 'free'.

By Potsdam the mood had soured. Roosevelt was dead — Truman replaced him.

The atomic bomb had been tested. Truman was tougher with Stalin. In March 1946 Churchill warned of an 'Iron Curtain' falling across Europe.

Ideological incompatibility plus mutual suspicion after WWII — disputes over Eastern Europe, the atomic bomb, and broken wartime agreements.
Stalin started it by invading Eastern Europe after the war.

mcqs.q: What did the Truman Doctrine commit the US to in 1947?
options: The Truman Doctrine ordered the dropping of the atomic bomb on Japan.
The Berlin Wall was built by NATO to keep East Germans out of West Germany.
Supporting free peoples resisting communist takeover — initially Greece and Turkey — formalising the policy of containment articulated by George Kennan.
The Truman Doctrine declared war on the Soviet Union.

mcqs.q: Why was the Berlin Wall built in 1961?
options: The Berlin Wall was built by NATO to keep East Germans out of West Germany.
To stop the mass flow of East Germans to the West via Berlin (millions had fled), which was draining the GDR of skilled workers and threatening the regime's survival.
The Berlin Wall was built to stop a Western invasion of East Berlin.
The Truman Doctrine ordered the dropping of the atomic bomb on Japan.
